c.tagline: Cobblestoned colonial time capsule where pastel mansions meet Caribbean beaches

taxi.color: pink/yellow classic cars & modern private taxis
taxi.fareNote: Meters are essentially nonexistent; agree on a price in cash (USD/EUR preferred) before you get in. Vintage American cars double as shared 'colectivo' taxis on fixed routes.

emergency.note: Police 106, ambulance 104, fire 105. Bring your own basic medical supplies — pharmacies are frequently under-stocked; travel insurance covering medical evacuation is strongly advised.

avoid.reason: Persistent jineteros (street hustlers) push commissions on casas and restaurants, and cobbled streets are poorly lit at night.

hood_desc: The UNESCO-listed historic heart: ochre cobblestones, terracotta roofs, and the mustard-yellow bell tower of the Convento de San Francisco. Museums, colonial mansions, and the main square anchor every visitor's first stop.
A quieter hillside quarter above the center, named for the small Ermita chapel, with sweeping views over Trinidad's rooftops to the Escambray Mountains. Fewer tourists, more everyday Trinidad life.
Home to grand 19th-century sugar-baron mansions like the Palacio Cantero, whose tower offers the best rooftop panorama in town. A mix of museums and family-run casas particulares.
Trinidad's after-dark hub, centered on the open-air stone steps of the Casa de la Música where locals and travelers dance to live son and salsa most nights under the stars.
A powder-white Caribbean beach about 12 km south of town, with turquoise water, beach clubs, and snorkeling — the classic day-trip pairing with Trinidad's colonial streets.

water.note: Stick to bottled or filtered water; supply and treatment are unreliable.

transit.map: No formal transit map; the historic center is small enough to walk end-to-end in 20 minutes
transit.note: There's no real public transit system in the historic center — walking, bici-taxis, and shared 'almendrones' (classic car colectivos) cover local trips, with a small tourist bus linking downtown to Playa Ancón.

air: Alberto Delgado Airport (TND, very limited/seasonal service)
José Martí International Airport, Havana (HAV, main gateway)
train: Historic Valle de los Ingenios tourist steam train (excursion only, not regular transport)
bus: Viazul tourist buses connect Havana, Cienfuegos, and Varadero to Trinidad

tip.r: Tipping is an essential part of Cuba's tourism economy where state wages are very low; 10% at restaurants, small cash tips for casa particular hosts, musicians, and guides are the norm.

landmarks: Plaza Mayor
The palm-studded heart of UNESCO-listed Trinidad, ringed by pastel colonial mansions and wrought-iron benches, glows golden against the Escambray mountains at sunset.
Iglesia Parroquial de la Santísima Trinidad
The city's stately parish church overlooking Plaza Mayor shelters the venerated Lord of the True Cross statue behind its serene neoclassical facade.
Museo Histórico Municipal (Palacio Cantero)
A sugar baron's frescoed mansion narrates Trinidad's slave-and-sugar fortunes, and its rooftop tower delivers the classic panorama of terracotta roofs and cobblestones.
Convento de San Francisco Bell Tower
Trinidad's most photographed landmark, this yellow-and-green bell tower rises above the Museum of the Struggle Against Bandits and the city's rippling rooftops.
Valle de los Ingenios and Manaca Iznaga Tower
A UNESCO valley of ruined sugar estates spreads below the 45-metre Iznaga tower, once used to watch enslaved workers across the cane fields.
Casa de la Música Steps
Each evening Trinidad gathers on these stone steps beside the church for live salsa, mojitos and dancing beneath the stars.
Palacio Brunet (Museo Romántico)
This aristocratic mansion on Plaza Mayor displays sumptuous 19th-century furnishings, crystal and porcelain evoking the refined excess of Trinidad's sugar aristocracy.
Playa Ancón
A ribbon of white sand and calm Caribbean water twelve kilometres from town, considered the finest beach on Cuba's southern coast.
Cerro de la Vigía and Ermita de la Popa
Climb past the ruined hilltop hermitage to Trinidad's radio mast summit for sweeping views over the city, valley and distant Caribbean.
Plaza Santa Ana
A quiet square northeast of the old town anchored by the ruined Iglesia Santa Ana and the former Real Cárcel prison, now a restaurant and souvenir shop.

train.note: Trinidad has no scheduled passenger train service. The surviving branch line through the Valle de los Ingenios is used by the heritage steam or diesel excursion to Manaca Iznaga, which leaves from the old station on Calle Lino Perez and runs only when locomotives and track allow - it is a sightseeing trip, not transport, and is frequently replaced by a bus. The nearest working railhead is Sancti Spiritus, about 70 km east, with slow Ferrocarriles de Cuba services from Havana every other day. Cuba has no international rail links of any kind.

bus.note: There are no international coaches from anywhere in Cuba. Viazul uses the terminal on Calle Piro Guinart at the western edge of the old town, an easy walk from Plaza Mayor, with several daily departures to Havana (about 6 hours), Cienfuegos (1.5 hours), Santa Clara, Varadero and a long run to Santiago de Cuba. Tickets are sold at the terminal counter for cash and the Havana services should be booked a day or two ahead in winter. Conectando hotel-to-hotel shuttles are sold through agencies, and shared taxis colectivos waiting outside the terminal will do Cienfuegos or Havana for a negotiated fare.

intl.to: Cayo Blanco & Cayo Macho (Cuba) - catamaran and launch excursions from Casilda port, about 6 km south of Trinidad
intl.op: Marina Trinidad excursion boats — tickets through Trinidad travel agencies

ferry.note: Trinidad's port is Casilda, about 6 km south towards Playa Ancon, where the Marina Trinidad runs day catamarans and launches out to the reef and the sandbar islands of Cayo Blanco and Cayo Macho. These are excursions rather than scheduled transport, sold through agencies in town and hotels on Playa Ancon, and they do not sail in bad weather. There is no scheduled passenger ferry from Casilda to anywhere else in Cuba and no international sailings.

half.name: Topes de Collantes
half.blurb: In the pine-scented Escambray mountains above town, waterfall trails like Salto del Caburní plunge through coffee plantations and lush cloud forest.
